title: A clearer route through the hull.
summary: The first engine assembly led to a selected cylinder-side exhaust route straight aft. The comparison records the component layout, compact-packaging goals and service-access checks still to complete.
dateLabel: 10 Oct 2026 · layout decision and packaging review
evidence: Selected packaging direction · fit and tuning pending

sections.title: Start with the complete installed system
sections.text: The first motion model established the mechanical relationships. The next question is how the engine, intake, starter, drive coupling and exhaust occupy the hull together. The rough Rhino assembly makes those space claims visible while exact purchased-part interfaces remain under verification. This is a packaging decision record, not a finished engine or a clearance approval.

sections.title: The first route: a loop around the engine
sections.text: Rev01 routed the exhaust forward around the engine before continuing aft. It provided a first space claim for the expansion volume and silencer, but also placed more exhaust envelope around the central assembly. Its segments are coarse, overlapping placeholders rather than a continuous manufactured pipe. The earlier model is retained so the change of direction remains visible.

sections.title: The selected route: cylinder side directly to the stern
sections.text: Following the founder’s 10 October routing sketch, Rev03 removes the forward loop and sends the exhaust aft from the cylinder side toward a stern outlet. This is the second routing option and the current selected direction. The pipe diameters, effective length, expansion profile, silencer and outlet height remain provisional; “selected” describes the route, not a final validated exhaust.

sections.title: Why compact packaging favours this direction
sections.text: The direct aft corridor avoids reserving forward-loop space around the engine. Our intent is to keep the central installation easier to arrange around the tank, battery, intake, starter and coupling. This is a qualitative packaging rationale: the study has not demonstrated a smaller complete installed volume, lower mass or higher power. A two-stroke exhaust must still provide the required acoustic length and expansion geometry; simply shortening a route is not a tuning method.

sections.title: Compact must also mean accessible
sections.text: The route is being developed to leave a practical approach to the engine through the hatch. We need room for plug and boot removal, starter servicing, head removal, fuel connections, coupling fasteners and extraction of the complete assembly. Fewer exhaust envelopes wrapped around the engine may help define those paths, but accessibility must be checked with the actual hatch and tools. A component fitting inside the outer hull does not establish that it can be installed, serviced or removed.

sections.title: What is in the first assembly
sections.text: The register below separates component groups and their evidence status. The downloadable Rev03 CSV lists every generated component, its layer and its nominal or assumed dimensions in millimetres. Off-the-shelf part identities remain in the component-selection record. CAD proxy dimensions must not be treated as supplier dimensions or procurement specifications.

sections.title: Alignment and clearance remain separate checks
sections.text: The pump and crankshaft alignment direction is the hull centre plane, with zero lateral shaft offset recorded in the routing study. Shaft height remains provisional. The preceding fit review reported mount isolators protruding below the outer hull, a silencer protrusion, an intake/exhaust overlap and a possible tank conflict. Rev03 changes the exhaust route but does not establish that all those issues are resolved. Inner-hull surfaces, laminate thickness, mount design and hatch geometry still need review.

sections.title: Thermal space, tuning and water protection
sections.text: A workable corridor needs separation from fuel components, intake, wiring and hoses, plus allowance for heat, vibration and hull movement. Outlet height, drainage and water-ingress protection must be developed as part of the installed system. Port timing and exhaust pressure-wave behaviour must be assessed together with gas temperature, effective acoustic length and engine load. None of these checks can be replaced by the rough routing picture.

sections.title: Preserve the decision and test the next revision
sections.text: Decision EXH-001 records the selected direct aft route, the compact-packaging and service-access intent, and unresolved checks. The next revision should verify inner-hull and hatch clearances, removal paths, mount positioning and thermal gaps, then replace envelopes with measured component geometry. Later gas-dynamics, bench and installed-hull tests will establish whether the design meets its functional requirements. Earlier layouts remain in the record. Follow-up · 10 October 2026: the chamber and water-jacket Rev01 baseline records the next dimensional study without establishing installed fit.
